# lazycommit

> lazycommit is a TypeScript CLI that uses Git and Groq to generate commit subjects from your staged changes. Choose a suggestion, edit it, regenerate it, or cancel before committing. The npm package is `lazycommitt` (double t). The commands are `lazycommit` and `lzc`.

Website: https://lazycommit.vercel.app
Source: https://github.com/KartikLabhshetwar/lazycommit
License: Apache-2.0

## Requirements

- Git
- Node.js 20.5 or newer
- A Groq API key from https://console.groq.com/keys (must start with `gsk_`)

## Install

```bash
npm install -g lazycommitt
```

Homebrew:

```bash
brew tap KartikLabhshetwar/lazycommit https://github.com/KartikLabhshetwar/lazycommit
brew install lazycommit
```

Set the API key and verify:

```bash
lazycommit config set GROQ_API_KEY="gsk_your_key_here"
lazycommit --version
```

Upgrade:

```bash
npm update -g lazycommitt
brew update
brew upgrade lazycommit
```

Use the first command for npm installs and the last two for Homebrew installs.

## Quick start

```bash
git add src/ README.md
lazycommit
```

The review menu offers Use as-is, Edit, Regenerate, and Cancel. Use as-is commits immediately. Edit shows a final confirmation before committing. The edited message must be one line.

To generate without committing:

```bash
lazycommit --dry-run
```

## Workflows

Conventional Commits 1.0.0 subjects (https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/), with an optional scope (a scope requires `--type conventional`). Edited messages must keep that format:

```bash
lazycommit --type conventional
lazycommit --type conventional --scope api --max-length 72
```

Multiple suggestions (1 to 5). Each suggestion is a separate request. Duplicates are removed, and failed requests can leave fewer suggestions than requested:

```bash
lazycommit --generate 3
```

Extra context and language:

```bash
lazycommit --context "Preserve existing login behavior while replacing session storage"
lazycommit --locale ja --type conventional
```

Preview (both need staged changes and reject `--all`):

```bash
lazycommit --preview-diff
lazycommit --dry-run --generate 3
```

`--preview-diff` prints the diff context locally, with no API key and no network request. `--dry-run` generates through Groq and prints only the subjects to stdout, one per line. Errors go to stderr.

Stage tracked changes or skip prompts:

```bash
lazycommit --all
lazycommit --yes
```

`--all` stages modified and deleted tracked files. It does not add untracked files. `--yes` commits the first valid suggestion without prompts. Without an interactive terminal, pass `--yes`, `--dry-run`, or `--preview-diff`.

## Large changes

Normal mode sends file statistics and the full included patch when it fits within `--max-diff-chars` (default 16000). Larger patches use bounded samples with omission markers.

```bash
lazycommit --max-diff-chars 24000
```

`--thorough` analyzes every included diff batch before generating:

```bash
lazycommit --thorough --type conventional --generate 3
lazycommit --preview-diff --thorough
```

Thorough mode divides the included diff and file statistics into batches of up to 16000 characters, asks the model to summarize each batch, combines the notes (summarizing further if needed), then generates and validates the final subjects. It uses more requests and takes longer. The input limit is 1.6 million characters. `--max-diff-chars` applies to normal mode only. Character budgets are not exact token counts.

## Generated files and exclusions

Lockfiles, minified files, and common build directories appear in the statistics, but their patches are omitted by default. Include them with `--include-generated`.

Exclude paths from statistics and code context with repeatable, repository-root Git pathspecs:

```bash
lazycommit --exclude 'dist/**' --exclude '*.log'
```

Exclusions affect analysis only. Excluded files that are staged are still committed. Binary changes and renames appear in the statistics. Binary contents are not interpreted.

## Flags

| Option | Behavior | Default and limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--generate`, `-g` | Number of suggestions | `1`, range 1 to 5 |
| `--type`, `-t` | Plain or conventional subject | Empty (plain) or `conventional` |
| `--scope` | Explicit conventional scope | Empty, up to 40 characters, requires conventional type |
| `--context` | Additional intent or constraints | Empty, one line, up to 2000 characters |
| `--locale` | Language of the subject | `en`, for example `ja` or `pt-BR` |
| `--model` | Groq model identifier | `openai/gpt-oss-20b` |
| `--max-length` | Maximum subject length | `100`, range 20 to 200 Unicode characters |
| `--max-diff-chars` | Normal-mode diff context budget | `16000`, range 1000 to 100000 |
| `--timeout` | Timeout per API request, in milliseconds | `10000`, range 500 to 300000 |
| `--thorough` | Analyze every included diff batch | Off |
| `--include-generated` | Include generated-file and lockfile patches | Off |
| `--exclude`, `-x` | Exclude a pathspec from analysis | Repeatable |
| `--all`, `-a` | Stage modifications and deletions in tracked files | Off |
| `--dry-run` | Generate subjects without committing | Off |
| `--preview-diff` | Print diff context without calling the API | Off |
| `--yes`, `-y` | Commit the first suggestion without prompts | Off |
| `--help`, `-h` | Show usage | None |
| `--version` | Show the installed version | None |

## Git options

Accepted Git options: `--signoff` (`-s`), `--no-signoff`, `--no-verify` (`-n`), `--author`, `--date`, `--trailer`, `--cleanup`, `--gpg-sign` (`-S`), `--no-gpg-sign`, `--quiet` (`-q`), `--verbose` (`-v`).

```bash
lazycommit --type conventional --signoff
lazycommit --author="Your Name <you@example.com>"
lazycommit --gpg-sign=YOUR_KEY_ID
```

Other options are rejected, including `-m`, `--amend`, and path arguments. Use `git commit` directly for those.

## Configuration

Settings live in `~/.lazycommit` (INI format, owner-only permissions requested).

```bash
lazycommit config set type=conventional max-length=72 generate=3
lazycommit config get model type max-length generate
lazycommit config set context="Preserve backward compatibility"
```

Clear an optional value by assigning an empty value:

```bash
lazycommit config set scope= context= proxy=
lazycommit config set type= scope=
```

Keys, defaults, and limits:

| Key | Default | Limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GROQ_API_KEY` | None (required) | Must start with `gsk_` |
| `model` | `openai/gpt-oss-20b` | No whitespace |
| `locale` | `en` | A locale code, for example `ja` or `pt-BR` |
| `generate` | `1` | Integer from 1 to 5 |
| `type` | Empty (plain) | Empty or `conventional` |
| `scope` | Empty | Up to 40 characters, requires conventional type |
| `context` | Empty | One line, up to 2000 characters |
| `max-length` | `100` | Integer from 20 to 200 |
| `max-diff-chars` | `16000` | Integer from 1000 to 100000 |
| `timeout` | `10000` | Integer from 500 to 300000, in milliseconds |
| `proxy` | None | An HTTP or HTTPS URL |

`--thorough`, `--yes`, and other workflow switches are per-invocation options and cannot be saved.

Precedence: generation flags override saved settings. `GROQ_API_KEY` in the environment overrides the saved key. Proxy environment variables override the saved proxy, checked in this order: `https_proxy`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `http_proxy`, `HTTP_PROXY`.

```bash
lazycommit config set proxy=http://localhost:8080
```

## Git hook

```bash
lazycommit hook install
git add src/
git commit
```

The hook generates a subject for review in your Git editor. With multiple suggestions, uncomment the one you want. For `git commit --no-edit` with an empty message file, it uses the first suggestion. An explicit message (`git commit -m "..."`) bypasses generation.

The hook uses normal-mode analysis, saved generation settings, and the same message validation as the CLI. Thorough analysis is CLI only. It installs to `.git/hooks/prepare-commit-msg` and does not support custom `core.hooksPath` locations or linked worktrees.

```bash
lazycommit hook uninstall
```

## How generation works

lazycommit snapshots the Git index and analyzes staged content, including partially staged files. Unstaged edits are not read into the prompt. It sends the selected diff context and your generation instructions to Groq. `--preview-diff` builds the context locally without sending it.

Subjects are checked for single-line output, length, and the requested format and scope. An invalid subject gets one more attempt. Subjects are not shortened by cutting off words. Transient API failures use the Groq SDK retry behavior (up to two retries).

Before a CLI commit, lazycommit checks that the staged tree and HEAD still match the analyzed snapshot. If either changed, it stops so you can rerun. The hook checks for staged-tree changes before writing its result.

Each run creates one commit with one subject line. Review the message for accuracy.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | What to try |
| --- | --- |
| No staged changes | Check `git diff --cached`. Stage files with `git add`, or use `--all` for tracked changes. Also check exclusions. |
| Interactive input is unavailable | Pass `--yes`, `--dry-run`, or `--preview-diff`. |
| Unsupported git argument | Only the accepted Git options work. Use `git commit` directly for `-m`, `--amend`, or paths. |
| A scope requires conventional type | Use `--type conventional`, or clear it with `lazycommit config set type= scope=`. |
| Subject is too vague | Add `--context`, try `--thorough`, or stage related changes separately. |
| No valid subject after retries | Increase `--max-length`, or choose another model available to your Groq account with `--model`. |
| Request too large (413) | In normal mode, lower `--max-diff-chars`. In either mode, exclude unnecessary files or stage smaller commits. |
| Rate limit (429) | Wait before retrying, reduce `--generate`, or leave thorough mode off. |
| Request timed out | Increase `--timeout`, for example `--timeout 30000`, and check connectivity. |
| Authentication error (401 or 403) | Check your API key and the model permissions for that key. |
| Staged content changed during review | Rerun lazycommit to analyze the current index. |
| Unknown option after installation | Check `lazycommit --version` and `--help`. Your release may be older than the docs. |

## Privacy and cost

Only the selected diff context and generation instructions (format, scope, language, length limit, and `--context`) are sent to Groq. In thorough mode, every included diff batch is sent for summarizing. Lockfile and generated-file patches are omitted unless `--include-generated` is set. Use `--preview-diff` to inspect the context locally.

Usage is billed by Groq under your API key. See https://groq.com/pricing. Request count grows with `--generate`, `--thorough`, and Regenerate.
